findings.claim: §11.10 describes break-glass as a two-gate process ('a paired DECISIONS row + waiver') while §12.7.4 defines a three-gate model (CODEOWNERS approval + D-NNN row + waivers.json entry). §11.10 was not updated when §12.7.4 was authored. After this PR merges, ADOPT-001 contains two inconsistent break-glass descriptions in the same document.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §11.10, 'When not to use rule-config', final bullet: 'One-off PR exceptions — use scp_bypass: true on the workflow invocation with a paired DECISIONS row + waiver per the §11.x break-glass procedure.' This enumerates exactly two gates. ADOPT-001 §12.7.4 'Break-glass procedure (three-gate model)': 'the PR must satisfy ALL THREE gates simultaneously: (1) Approving review from a member of SCP-CODEOWNERS … (2) Sibling D-NNN row … (3) Matching waivers.json entry … Any miss → SCP-E004 → merge-blocked.' The CODEOWNERS approval gate (gate 1) is absent from §11.10.
findings.impact: An adopter reading §11.10 (the rule-config section they are most likely to encounter first) gets an incomplete picture of break-glass requirements. They prepare a D-NNN row and waivers.json entry, invoke scp_bypass: true, and receive SCP-E004 from the CODEOWNERS gate that §11.10 never mentioned. This is a documentation defect in a security-enforcement procedure; the cost is a blocked PR that the adopter cannot self-diagnose from the docs they read.
findings.mitigation: In this PR, amend §11.10's break-glass pointer to read: 'One-off PR exceptions — use scp_bypass: true on the workflow invocation with a paired DECISIONS row + waiver per the three-gate break-glass procedure in §12.7.4.' Replace 'paired DECISIONS row + waiver' with the three-gate summary or a direct cross-reference. This is a one-line edit in the same file and should not require a separate PR.

findings.claim: §11.10 contains the cross-reference '§11.x break-glass procedure' which does not resolve to any section in ADOPT-001. The intended target is now §12.7.4 (published by this slice), but §11.10 was not updated. Every adopter following §11.10's pointer will encounter a dangling reference.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §11.10, 'When not to use rule-config': '… per the §11.x break-glass procedure.' ADOPT-001 contains sections §11.1 through §11.10 and §12.1 through §12.7. There is no §11.x sub-section; the label is a placeholder that was not resolved when §12.7 was authored. The correct target section is §12.7.4 'Break-glass procedure (three-gate model)'.
findings.impact: ADOPT-001 is the canonical onboarding doc for WP-SCP-024 estate cascade. A dangling §11.x reference in the production version of this doc will confuse every adopter who attempts to follow the break-glass path from §11.10. The reference is in a 'when not to use' guidance block — adopters who comply and need an exception will hit the dangling pointer at exactly the moment they need the procedure.
findings.mitigation: In this PR, replace '§11.x break-glass procedure' in §11.10 with '§12.7.4 break-glass procedure (three-gate model)'. This edit fixes both COMP-MAJ-001 and COMP-MAJ-002 simultaneously if combined into a single rewording of the §11.10 bullet.

findings.claim: The forward-looking SECURITY.md item (§12.7.8) names 'WP-SCP-020 §4.1 follow-up SCP-073.sec' as the delivery vehicle, but SCP-073.sec does not appear in STATUS.md's post-Threshold-A backlog or the open scheduled follow-ups table. The audit trail for this deferred item is broken.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.8: 'Adopters concerned about a policy-bypass disclosure should follow the SCP repo's SECURITY.md policy … (when published — WP-SCP-020 §4.1 follow-up SCP-073.sec).' DISPATCH-NOTE 'Forward-looking flags': 'SECURITY.md — §12.7.8; lands in WP-SCP-020 §4.1 follow-up SCP-073.sec.' STATUS.md post-Threshold-A backlog lists: 020G (struck through as presumably landed before 020H part 3), 020H part 3, 020H.1, WP-SCP-022 proposal-queue, WP-SCP-023, WP-SCP-024. SCP-073.sec is not listed. STATUS.md open scheduled follow-ups table also contains no SCP-073.sec entry. WP-SCP-020 §4.1 deferred table lists 'Follow-up SCP-073.sec | SECURITY.md embargo path' but this is the plan doc, not the live STATUS.
findings.impact: Unlike 020H.1 and rule-regression (both listed in STATUS.md's backlog), SCP-073.sec has no live tracking entry. If this PR merges without adding SCP-073.sec to STATUS.md, the SECURITY.md publication has no durable reminder and may never land. Adopters reading §12.7.8 are directed to a URL for a document that has no committed delivery path in the live project tracking.
findings.mitigation: Add 'SCP-073.sec: SECURITY.md publication (security disclosure path for policy-bypass reports)' to STATUS.md's post-Threshold-A backlog in this PR. Alternatively, add it to the open scheduled follow-ups table with a target date tied to 020H.1 (since it is a parallel track). Either approach creates a durable trail that the post-merge STATUS.md commitment (which the DISPATCH-NOTE defers to the next slice's PR) cannot omit.

findings.claim: §12.7 provides no 'verify the integration is working' acceptance step. An adopter who completes §12.7.1 through §12.7.3 has no documented way to confirm the gate is live before relying on it for production PRs.
findings.evidence: §12.7.1 documents the wrapper YAML. §12.7.2 documents the Renovate extends entry. §12.7.3 documents the enable-required-check.sh helper and mentions '--plan first to see both the current state and the proposed payload.' None of these sub-sections includes an explicit 'open a draft PR with a deliberate violation and confirm the gate blocks merge' or 'run gh api to verify the required-check context is registered' step. The adoption acceptance checklist in §15 covers the overall SCP onboarding but does not include a federation-primitive-specific verification step (e.g., verify the policy-check / scp/policy-check context appears in branch protection after running the helper).
findings.impact: Adopters may complete all setup steps and assume they are protected when the required-check context name does not match (a real failure mode documented in D-033: the bare scp/policy-check context does not match the rendered Actions check-run name policy-check / scp/policy-check). Without a verification step, this misconfiguration is invisible until a real violation slips through. The D-033 episode on SCP self demonstrates that the naming issue is non-obvious and requires empirical confirmation.
findings.mitigation: Add a §12.7.3.x (or paragraph within §12.7.3) titled 'Verify the gate is live' with: (a) the gh api command from docs/security/branch-protection.md §How to verify adapted for the adopter's repo (substitute the adopter's rendered context name); (b) instruction to open a test PR with a deliberate SCP-R-001 violation (a services.yml with an invalid auth mode) and confirm the gate blocks merge before relying on it in production. Cross-reference D-033 as the rationale for empirical verification.

findings.claim: §12.7.5 documents only per-release SHA-pin rollback (revert wrapper @SHA + re-run Renovate). There is no documented path for removing the entire federation-primitive integration. An adopter who decides to de-adopt SCP mid-stream has no documented removal procedure.
findings.evidence: §12.7.5 'Rollback procedure': '1. Revert the wrapper's @SHA pin to the previous SCP release SHA via PR. 2. Update the # tag: comment to match. 3. Renovate will re-run the bump … 4. Open an issue using the rule-regression template.' All four steps assume the adopter wants to stay on an older SCP release, not exit the integration entirely. There is no instruction covering: remove .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, remove the extends entry from renovate.json, and run enable-required-check.sh with a removal flag (or manually remove the required-check via gh api) to un-gate the branch protection.
findings.impact: The plan's §8 risk row 'Rego false-positive cascade' and §8's 'SCP-outage blast radius' both assume adopters can revert to a safe state quickly (target 4h, §12.7.5 iv-e). A false-positive cascade affecting multiple rules simultaneously may make per-release rollback insufficient if the regression was in the workflow infrastructure itself. Without a full-removal path, an adopter in that scenario has no documented escape route. For WP-SCP-024 estate cascade adopters, this gap is systemic across all six target repos.
findings.mitigation: Add §12.7.5 step 5 (or a separate sub-section '§12.7.5.1 Full de-adoption'): (a) delete .github/workflows/policy-check.yml via PR; (b) remove the extends entry from renovate.json via the same PR; (c) after merge, run: gh api -X DELETE repos/OWNER/NAME/branches/BRANCH/protection/required_status_checks/contexts -F contexts[]='{rendered-context-name}' or use the GitHub UI to remove the required check; (d) document the de-adoption in a D-NNN row in the repo's DECISIONS equivalent. This documents the escape route without weakening the normal rollback path.

findings.claim: §12.7.4 discloses the single-operator constraint only for adopter-side governance ('Single-operator adopters: … self-approval is structurally impossible on GitHub; document this in your repo's analogue of WP-SCP-020 §8') but does not disclose that SCP's own source — the reusable workflow and Renovate preset the adopter is extending — is itself operated under an identical single-operator constraint per D-031. An adopter cannot make an informed adoption-risk decision without knowing the supply-chain source is single-operator-gated.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.4 break-glass text: 'Single-operator adopters: per WP-SCP-020 §8 + D-031 (single-operator personal-account closure), self-approval is structurally impossible on GitHub; document this in your repo's analogue of WP-SCP-020 §8 + 2026-07-21 quarterly review.' This advises adopters about their own single-operator situation. D-031 in DECISIONS.md: 'Apply WP-SCP-020 slice 020K on the SCP repository in the personal-account / single-operator mode … (a) NO scp-break-glass GitHub team is created … CODEOWNERS names @jrnb2024 only.' The SCP-side single-operator constraint is not surfaced to adopters reading §12.7. The 2026-07-21 quarterly review is mentioned as a reference only for the adopter's own governance, not as SCP's own re-evaluation checkpoint.
findings.impact: An adopter with governance requirements around supply-chain single-operator risk (e.g. a regulated-sector adopter or one with multiple maintainers who want two-person integrity on the gate source) cannot evaluate whether to adopt SCP's federation primitive without knowing the source is @jrnb2024-only. The WP-SCP-024 estate cascade will drive this appendix to six adopters; none of them will have this information unless they independently read D-031.
findings.mitigation: Add a 'SCP source — bus-factor-1 disclosure' paragraph to §12.7.4 (or §12.7, reference section): 'As of v1.0.0, the SCP reusable workflow and Renovate preset (the source this integration depends on) are operated by a single maintainer (@jrnb2024) per D-031 (WP-SCP-020 §8 bus-factor-1 risk row). The quarterly bus-factor-1 review is scheduled for 2026-07-21. Adopters with multi-maintainer or regulatory requirements for supply-chain diversity should note this constraint and re-evaluate at that checkpoint.' This is a factual disclosure, not a descope.

findings.claim: The DISPATCH-NOTE post-merge commitment to 'mark TF-D1-001..003 closed in the tracked-forward section' of STATUS.md is unachievable as stated: STATUS.md's tracked-forward section lists only TF-005..008 (from 020C.1). TF-D1-001..003 do not appear in that section. The commitment requires an implicit add-then-close in a future PR with no current trail in STATUS.md.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE §'Post-merge STATUS.md update commitment': 'The Tracked-forward items section: mark TF-D1-001..003 closed (or add a "Closed in 020H part 3" annotation row).' STATUS.md §'Tracked-forward items from 020C.1': lists TF-005, TF-006, TF-007, TF-008 only. TF-D1-001..003 are not listed anywhere in STATUS.md's tracked-forward section; they appear only in docs/releases/v1.0.0-rc.1.md §'Known limitations / tracked-forward items'. The DISPATCH-NOTE itself defers both STATUS.md edits to 'the next slice's PR (likely 020H.1)' — meaning 020H part 3 merges without the updates, and if 020H.1 is delayed or scoped differently, the closure evidence evaporates.
findings.impact: Post-merge auditability of TF-D1-001..003 closure depends on a future PR (020H.1) performing a non-obvious compound operation (add entries AND mark closed) on STATUS.md's tracked-forward section. If 020H.1 is dispatched without explicitly including this task, or if a future reviewer reads STATUS.md to confirm TF-D1-002 (fork-PR refusal as mandatory) is closed, they find no entry and cannot resolve the claim. The DISPATCH-NOTE's statement 'Bundle both edits with the next slice's PR to keep the chain auditable' introduces a dependency chain gap rather than eliminating one.
findings.mitigation: In this PR, add TF-D1-001, TF-D1-002, TF-D1-003 to STATUS.md's tracked-forward section with status 'Closed in 020H part 3 (PR #NNN)'. If the PR number is not yet known at authorship time, add them as 'Closed — see docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020h3/DISPATCH-NOTE.md'. This makes the closure self-evidencing at merge time and removes the dependency on 020H.1 for historical accuracy. The DISPATCH-NOTE's bundling guidance for STATUS.md is acceptable for the backlog-table row (marking 020H part 3 landed), but the tracked-forward closure should be in this PR's diff.

findings.claim: §12.7 presents sub-sections in logical order but provides no explicit step-sequenced order-of-operations for a new adopter. A first-time integrator must infer the sequence (add wrapper → add Renovate extends → run enable-required-check.sh → verify gate → understand break-glass) from sub-section ordering alone.
findings.evidence: §12.7.1 (wrapper), §12.7.2 (Renovate), §12.7.3 (branch-protection helper) are in correct order but carry no 'Step 1 / Step 2 / Step 3' framing. §12.7.4 (break-glass) and §12.7.5 (rollback) are reference procedures, not setup steps, but this distinction is not stated. WP-SCP-024 estate cascade will use this appendix to onboard FLA, PIM, recommender, shopify-app, mapp-doc-agent, and control-tower; operator familiarity with GitHub Actions onboarding varies across those teams.
findings.impact: A new adopter who reads §12.7 in sequence without framing may attempt to run enable-required-check.sh before adding the wrapper (if §12.7.3 feels like step 1 independently), or may skip the Renovate preset assuming it is optional. The order matters because the required-check must reference a check that has already been observed (GitHub only accepts a context name that exists in the repo's check history). Wrong order → required-check points to a non-existent context → permanent 'Expected — Waiting'.
findings.mitigation: Add a brief 'Setup sequence' paragraph at the top of §12.7 (before §12.7.1): 'Perform these steps in order: (1) Add the caller wrapper (§12.7.1) and merge at least one PR so GitHub registers the check-run context. (2) Add the Renovate preset (§12.7.2). (3) Run the branch-protection helper (§12.7.3) — only after at least one successful check-run has been observed. (4) Confirm the gate is live (verify step — see §12.7.3). §12.7.4–§12.7.12 are reference sections consulted as needed.' Four sentences; no descoping.

findings.claim: The label 'SCP-CODEOWNERS' in §12.7.4 gate 1 reads as a reference to SCP's own CODEOWNERS file (a specific GitHub file in the jrnb2024/standards-control-plane- repo) but the parenthetical clarifies it means 'your repo's CODEOWNERS for paths matching the gate's domain'. This terminology collision will cause confusion for WP-SCP-024 estate adopters unfamiliar with SCP's internal naming.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.4, gate 1: 'Approving review from a member of SCP-CODEOWNERS (your repo's CODEOWNERS for paths matching the gate's domain — typically services.yml, output/findings/waivers.json, or policies/** if you mirror locally).' The backtick formatting of SCP-CODEOWNERS makes it look like a literal file or group name. An adopter naturally reads 'SCP-CODEOWNERS' as referring to the SCP project's own CODEOWNERS set (i.e., @jrnb2024 must review every break-glass bypass in every adopter repo), which is wrong — it is the adopter's own CODEOWNERS configuration that matters.
findings.impact: An adopter who misreads gate 1 as requiring @jrnb2024's review will either (a) conclude the procedure is unworkable (an external party must approve every adopter's bypass) or (b) attempt to contact @jrnb2024 for break-glass approval on their own repo's PRs. Either outcome blocks the adopter's governance process unnecessarily.
findings.mitigation: Rewrite gate 1 label: 'Approving review from a member listed in your repo's CODEOWNERS for the paths the bypass affects (typically services.yml, output/findings/waivers.json, or your local policy mirror if you maintain one; configure these in your CODEOWNERS analogously to how SCP's break-glass governance is configured per D-031).' Dropping the backtick-wrapped SCP-CODEOWNERS label removes the collision.

findings.claim: The plan §4 020H part 3 canonical wrapper spec text still shows 'jrnb2024/standards-control-plane' (no trailing dash) in both the uses: line and the Renovate marker comment. TF-D1-001 was correctly resolved in ADOPT-001's §12.7.1, but the plan spec text is now a permanently misleading authoritative reference. Future authors reading WP-SCP-020 §4 to produce downstream adopter docs (WP-SCP-024 scaffolder, etc.) may propagate the typo.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 3 canonical YAML block: '# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane' and 'uses: jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@…'. ADOPT-001 §12.7.1 correctly shows 'depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-' and 'uses: jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-/.github/workflows/…'. The DISPATCH-NOTE acknowledges TF-D1-001 as closed in ADOPT-001 but does not note that the plan spec text remains wrong. docs/releases/v1.0.0-rc.1.md and the live policy-check-wrapper.yml both correctly use the trailing dash.
findings.impact: WP-SCP-020 is the governing specification document for all federation-primitive work. A scaffolding author who reads §4 020H part 3's canonical YAML as the template for scripts/scaffold-downstream.sh (per SCP-073-scaffolder) will produce wrappers pointing at the wrong repo name — a silent failure because jrnb2024/standards-control-plane (without dash) does not exist and GitHub will return a 404, fail-closing the entire gate infrastructure in adopter repos.
findings.mitigation: In the next plan amendment opportunity (020H.1 dispatch or a governance-only PR), update WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 3's canonical YAML block to add the trailing dash to both the depName and the uses: path. Add a note: 'Corrected from plan-v0.6 per TF-D1-001 closure in 020H part 3.' This is a spec-doc amendment, not a code change, and can be bundled with the next planned plan update.

findings.claim: §12.7.4 break-glass gate 1 parenthetical lists SCP-internal paths (services.yml, output/findings/waivers.json, policies/**) as examples of what CODEOWNERS should cover. Estate adopters (FLA, PIM, recommender, shopify-app, mapp-doc-agent, control-tower) have different sensitive artifact paths; the SCP-internal examples will lead adopters to configure CODEOWNERS coverage for non-existent paths.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.4 gate 1: '… typically services.yml, output/findings/waivers.json, or policies/** if you mirror locally.' services.yml and output/findings/waivers.json are SCP-specific artifact paths. FLA and PIM may have different findings/waivers storage locations; mapp-doc-agent and control-tower have no SCP output/ tree at all unless they adopt one. The 'if you mirror locally' qualifier for policies/** is the only generic-qualified path.
findings.impact: Low — the parenthetical is illustrative, not prescriptive, and the 'typically' qualifier partially mitigates the specificity. However, WP-SCP-024 estate cascade operators applying this appendix verbatim will add CODEOWNERS rules that cover paths that do not exist in their repo, producing vacuous CODEOWNERS rules and a false sense of governance coverage.
findings.mitigation: Generalise the parenthetical to: '… typically the paths where your waivers.json, findings, and any locally-mirrored policy files live (for SCP-self: services.yml, output/findings/waivers.json; configure for your repo's equivalent artifact paths).' One sentence addition; no descoping.

findings.claim: §12.7.2 states the Renovate preset is 'published at renovate/v1.0.0 (independent of the federation-primitive v* tag series)' without a one-sentence rationale for the independence. An adopter who does not read docs/security/branch-protection.md may conflate a renovate/v1.1.0 preset release with a v1.1.0 workflow release and misinterpret Renovate PRs that bump only the preset ref.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.2: 'The preset is published at renovate/v1.0.0 (independent of the federation-primitive v* tag series; see docs/security/branch-protection.md).' The cross-reference to branch-protection.md is present but that document explains the ruleset mechanics, not the tag-independence rationale. docs/security/branch-protection.md §'Tag protection — renovate/v* pattern': 'The two rulesets are siblings, not nested. The v* ruleset covers federation-primitive release tags. The renovate/v* ruleset covers preset release tags.' Still no rationale for why they are independent.
findings.impact: Minor. An adopter who receives a Renovate PR bumping renovate/v1.0.0 → renovate/v1.1.0 but not the @SHA pin may approve it expecting a workflow rule update and find none, or reject it thinking it is incomplete. The Renovate PR title/body should clarify, but the appendix does not prepare adopters for this scenario.
findings.mitigation: Add one sentence to §12.7.2 after the independence note: 'The tag series are independent because preset configuration changes (customManager regex adjustments, automerge policy, datasource options) may need to ship without a new workflow release, and vice versa — a v1.1.0 Rego rule change ships a v1.1.0 workflow tag without necessarily changing the Renovate preset.' This is a documentation addition, not a scope change.

findings.claim: §12.7.9 pre-commit hook snippet uses the placeholder 'exec <your-local-clone-of-standards-control-plane>/scripts/scp-policy-check' with no guidance on where to maintain the clone, how to keep it updated, or whether the local clone should be pinned to the same SHA as the CI wrapper. The 'optional, recommended' qualifier reduces urgency, but the placeholder is incomplete for a new adopter.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.9: 'cat > .git/hooks/pre-commit <<'EOF' … exec <your-local-clone-of-standards-control-plane>/scripts/scp-policy-check'. No subsequent note explains: (a) typical clone location (e.g. ~/src/standards-control-plane- or a submodule); (b) whether the clone's checked-out SHA should match the CI wrapper's pinned SHA for exact parity; (c) that an outdated local clone would evaluate against a different rule version than CI, defeating local reproduction. The local-reproduction guarantee in §12.7.6 (Python vs Rego parity via conflict-gate) and in scripts/scp-policy-check (same lib/policy_check_invocation.sh) assumes the same-SHA clone constraint, but this is not stated in §12.7.9.
findings.impact: Trivial for adopters who can infer from context. Non-trivial for WP-SCP-024 estate adopters whose setup is driven by a scaffolding script — if the scaffolding script copies §12.7.9 verbatim, it produces a pre-commit hook with a literal angle-bracket path that fails chmod execution.
findings.mitigation: Add two sentences below the hook snippet: 'Replace <your-local-clone-of-standards-control-plane> with the absolute path to a local clone of the SCP repo. Pin the local clone to the same commit SHA as your CI wrapper's uses: line to guarantee the pre-commit hook evaluates against the same rule version as CI.'
